title: Exact normalized transport of constant left modules
statement: For arbitrary small sites J and K, a ring Λ (not assumed commutative), a geometric adjunction L ⊣ R on set sheaves, and preservation of finite limits by L, there is a lift ConstantLeftModuleInverseImageLift J K Λ L R adj hL. Its fields specify the normalized constant-ring comparison, transported abelian and scalar operations, module adjunction and its forgotten unit, and additivity and preservation of finite limits and colimits. The notions are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Construct the terminal comparison for the constant singleton sheaf using preservation of terminal objects. The global-sections/coyoneda identification and the original adjunction identify the right adjoints of constantSheaf J ⋙ L and constantSheaf K. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives a comparison natural in every coefficient type. Compose its component at Λ with constantCommuteCompose to get ringUnderlying; naturality at each singleton-to-Λ map gives constant_scalar.

proof.text: For a binary ring operation, identify the constant sheaf on Λ × Λ with the product of the underlying constant ring sheaves. Its two projections are the constant projections followed by the inverse forgetful comparison; the product comparison of constantSheaf is invertible. Precomposition with this isomorphism reduces the operation to its value on constant sections, by sheafify_hom_ext and the ring-homomorphism laws of toSheafify. Naturality of the constant comparison, checked on projections, therefore proves ring_add and ring_mul in the given order.

proof.text: For a left exact functor from an additive category to set sheaves, apply AddCommGrpCat.leftExactFunctorForgetEquivalence at every section. Its fully faithful forgetful functor lifts the restriction maps and natural transformations, and its counit is definitionally the identity on underlying sets. This constructs abelianInverse and abelianDirect with their set comparisons. Lift the set-level unit and counit by the same full faithfulness; their triangle identities follow by faithful forgetting, comparison naturality, and the original triangles. Addition transport follows from the formula prodComparison U ≫ addition = U.map (prod.fst + prod.snd) and additivity of left exact functors.

source.place: Tag 00YV, finite-product transport and fixed-ring scalar-endomorphism proof; realized by the Mathlib APIs named in the step

proof.text: For each constant-ring module M and scalar r, form the abelian endomorphism scalarEndo M r. Its one, zero, addition, multiplication, and naturality identities hold sectionwise. Applying either additive abelian lift gives an ordinary Λ-module on every target section; naturality gives restriction maps linear over the constant ring presheaf. Apply PresheafOfModules.sheafify with α = toSheafify of the constant ring and the identity map on the underlying abelian sheaf. This extends the scalar action to the sheafified constant ring without changing the abelian sheaf. PresheafOfModules.toSheafify proves that constant scalars act by the transported scalar endomorphisms, and sheafifyMap constructs the functor on morphisms.

source.place: Tag 00YV, finite-product transport and fixed-ring scalar-endomorphism proof; realized by the Mathlib APIs named in the step

proof.text: The abelian adjunction unit and counit commute with every scalarEndo by their naturality. PresheafOfModules.restrictHomEquivOfIsLocallySurjective applied to the constant-ring sheafification extends this constant-scalar linearity to linearity over every coefficient section. Thus the same unit and counit lift to module sheaves. Faithful forgetting proves their naturality and triangle identities. Their underlying maps give the required unit_compatibility and abelian_unit equations.

source.place: Tag 00YV, finite-product transport and fixed-ring scalar-endomorphism proof; realized by the Mathlib APIs named in the step

proof.text: The module functor preserves finite limits because its composite with the faithful forgetful functor to abelian sheaves is the composite of two finite-limit-preserving functors, and forgetting reflects limits. Its additivity is checked after faithful forgetting using additivity of the abelian lift. The module adjunction gives preservation of colimits and hence finite colimits. Assemble these constructions and the normalized coefficient comparison into the unchanged lift structure.
